title: rootless: clear environment before spawning pause process
body:
<!-- Please include a concise description of your changes -->
### Description
When spawning the pause process in `pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.c`, the process inherited environment variables from the parent process before setting `_PODMAN_PAUSE=1`. If the parent environment exceeded 4096 bytes (the chunk size read by `is_pause_process`), `_PODMAN_PAUSE=1` was placed beyond the first 4KB chunk, causing `is_pause_process` to treat a healthy pause process as stale and unlink its `pause.pid` file.

This PR calls `clearenv()` before setting `_PODMAN_PAUSE=1` so the pause process only carries the necessary marker at index 0. Additionally, `is_pause_process()` safely null-terminates its read buffer.

Fixes: #29650
Signed-off-by: sundeep8967 <sundeep8967@gmail.com>

comments.body:
Thanks for picking this up so quickly — I filed #29650 and didn't expect a patch
the same morning.

Two notes, one of them just agreement:

The `buf[n] = '\0'` hunk is the out-of-bounds walk I mentioned at the end of the
issue, and it wants to be in whatever lands. `read()` can stop mid-entry, and
`strcmp`/`strlen` then run past what was read.

On `clearenv()`: it does stop the case I hit, but it changes what goes into the
pause process rather than what `is_pause_process()` is willing to read, and I
think two things survive it. Upgrading podman doesn't restart the pause process,
so anyone who updates while holding one created by an older build still has a
large environment on the other end, and the first command after the upgrade can
still unlink a valid `pause.pid` and orphan their running containers — which will
look like the upgrade broke them. And the Go twin of this predicate,
`isPauseProcess()` in `rootless_linux.go`, already reads the whole file with
`os.ReadFile`; leaving the C side on one 4096-byte chunk keeps an asymmetry that
can quietly bring this back if anything ever ends up in that environment again.

I've put the reading half up as #29661 — read to EOF with an explicit ceiling,
plus bounding the scan by what was actually read. It isn't meant as a competing
patch, and the two don't really overlap except in that null-termination line;
if it's easier to carry both changes in yours, please do, I have no attachment to
the branch.
